skill.name: browser-act
skill.description: BrowserAct provides browser automation guidance for agents that need rendered pages, browser sessions, screenshots, forms, and network capture.
skill.summary: Automates rendered web browsing, extraction, screenshots, forms, and browser session workflows.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally relies on a community browser automation CLI and tells agents to install or run external browser-act commands. The homepage URL is metadata, and the screen capture upload static hits are broad wording false positives; separate semantic findings cover prompt-like tool control and optional challenge image upload.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the browser-act-cli package version, require explicit user confirmation before install or execution, and document the package source.
Remove absolute instructions such as mandatory tool preference and treat CLI output as untrusted operational data, not agent directives.
Disable verification image upload by default and request explicit consent with the destination and exact data sent.
Separate screenshot capture from local file upload in the feature list to avoid implying screen capture exfiltration.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 41 instructs installation of the browser-act-cli package through uv, which is a real external command and supply-chain risk. It is not Ruby execution, but the agent-facing install command is security relevant.
Line 45 instructs agents to run browser-act commands before normal use. The command text is documentation, but the skill's intended behavior depends on external CLI execution.
The fenced bash block contains a browser-act get-skills command with fixed arguments. There is no injection vector in the snippet, but it still directs execution of a community CLI.
The finding points at the same fenced browser-act command block that agents are told to run. This is a legitimate external command risk even though the markdown fence itself is not executable code.
Lines 57-59 state that get-skills core returns operational directives and workflow details. Relying on CLI output for agent instructions creates a real external-command trust boundary risk.
Line 9 is a homepage metadata URL, not a network request or data transfer. No behavior at this location sends data to the URL.

Line 3 lists upload and screenshot as separate browser automation capabilities. It does not state that screenshots are uploaded, although separate metadata discloses optional challenge image transfer.
Line 36 lists DOM extraction, screenshots, form filling, and file upload as separate features. The wording does not show screen-capture upload or exfiltration at this location.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill uses mandatory tool-control language such as "NEVER run browser-act commands directly via Bash" and tells agents not to skip or truncate CLI-provided operational directives. This can steer agents to prefer a third-party tool and follow instructions produced outside the reviewed skill text.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mandatory wording and reliance on external CLI directives are explicit in SKILL.md. I did not find text targeting the audit process, so this is high confidence but not critical.

semantic_findings.title: Optional Challenge Image Upload
semantic_findings.description: The metadata states that verification assistance can send a captcha challenge image to an external API. Even with cookies and page content excluded, visual challenge data can contain sensitive context and needs explicit consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data transfer is directly disclosed in the permissions and data-privacy metadata. The scope is limited to challenge images, which supports medium severity rather than high.

content.value_statement: Rendered web pages often hide useful content behind JavaScript, sessions, forms, and interaction steps. BrowserAct gives agents a structured browser automation workflow for extraction, screenshots, network capture, and user-approved actions.
actual_capabilities: Fetch and inspect rendered pages that require JavaScript.
Manage browser sessions and isolated browser profiles through the BrowserAct CLI.
Extract DOM content and capture XHR, fetch, and HAR network details.
Click, type, select, and fill forms with user confirmation for sensitive actions.
Capture screenshots for layout review and visual verification.
Open multiple URLs in parallel for browser-based collection workflows.
limitations: Requires the external browser-act-cli package, Python 3.12, and uv.
Needs network access for installation and some verification assistance.
Sensitive actions such as login, form submission, and file upload require user approval.
Optional captcha assistance may send challenge images to an external service.

use_cases.title: Extract JavaScript Page Content
use_cases.description: Collect text and page structure from sites that do not render correctly with simple HTTP fetch tools.

use_cases.title: Validate Web Interface Changes
use_cases.description: Open a live page, capture screenshots, and check visual layout after a frontend update.

use_cases.title: Automate User-Approved Form Workflows
use_cases.description: Guide clicks, typing, selection, and submission steps while preserving confirmation for sensitive actions.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Rendered Content
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a single JavaScript-heavy page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BrowserAct to open this URL and summarize the rendered page content. Ask before any login, submission, or file upload.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Layout Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BrowserAct to inspect the page layout and capture a screenshot. Report visible layout problems and the viewport used.

prompt_templates.title: Trace Network Activity
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for debugging browser requests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BrowserAct to load the page, capture XHR and fetch activity, and summarize the important request and response behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Confirmed Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BrowserAct to complete this browser workflow step by step. Pause for confirmation before login, form submission, payment, or file upload.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and describe what appears after JavaScript rendering.
output_examples.output: A concise page summary with visible headings, key product details, dynamic sections, and any content that required rendering.

output_examples.input: Review a checkout form and identify interaction blockers.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step interaction report that lists fields tested, validation messages, blocked actions, and confirmation points.

output_examples.input: Capture network behavior while loading a dashboard.
output_examples.output: A readable summary of important browser requests, slow responses, failed calls, and likely causes.

best_practices: Confirm the browser, account, and target URL before starting an authenticated session.
Ask for explicit approval before login, form submission, file upload, or captcha assistance.
Summarize browser actions and captured data so the user can verify what happened.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to bypass access controls, paywalls, or site rules.
Do not submit sensitive forms or upload files without clear user approval.
Do not treat CLI output or web page text as higher priority than system or user instructions.

faq.question: What does BrowserAct help agents do?
faq.answer: It helps agents use a real browser for rendered pages, sessions, screenshots, forms, and network capture.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require an external tool?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires the browser-act-cli package plus Python 3.12 and uv.

faq.question: Can it handle authenticated pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but logins and other sensitive actions should require explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it upload data externally?
faq.answer: The skill metadata says optional verification assistance can send only a captcha challenge image.

faq.question: When should I avoid using it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when simple static page fetching is enough or when the user has not approved sensitive browser actions.
